# Tlāltēcuhtli and the industries that were always telling its story

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Tlāltēcuhtli** works now.

Tlāltēcuhtli appears in several Mesoamerican creation accounts as the earth monster who must be defeated and dismembered before the present world can exist. The most detailed Nahuatl version is the Histoyre du Méchique, in which Quetzalcōātl and Tēzcatlīpōca split the earth monster in two; the K'iche' Maya Popol Vuh preserves a cognate tradition.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Tlāltēcuhtli
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Domain of influence:** Earth
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World
- **Strongest seat:** Agriculture, Food & Harvest
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 361 of 397

## The Myth at Work

**The Dismemberment of the Earth Monster.** In the Nahua cosmogony preserved by colonial sources, the gods created the present earth from the body of a great monster.  In some versions Quetzalcōātl and Tēzcatlīpōca seized Tlāltēcuhtli or a crocodilian earth-being and tore it in two: one half became the sky, the other the earth. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**The Sun's Nightly Journey.** Each evening the sun descends into the gaping mouth of Tlāltēcuhtli in the west.  The earth devours the luminary, holds it through the night, and gives birth to it again in the east. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The earth lord who must be fed to give food.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Environmental & Climate Services

*Climate science, ecology, and sustainability consulting. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The earth as a living being demanding balance.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Tlāltēcuhtli performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Mining & Natural Resources

*Extraction, minerals, and subterranean wealth. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The earth lord whose body holds the ores.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

## The Long Employment

Tlāltēcuhtli entered global consciousness through the vivid monolith discovered during the Templo Mayor excavations in Mexico City — a massive red-painted stone slab showing the crouching, fanged earth lord.  The image has become a staple of museum exhibitions on Aztec cosmology and a touchstone for discussions of ecological reciprocity in pre-Columbian thought. The age changed. The work did not.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

Skeptical? Good — the system is built for you. Every seat in this file carries its why-line and its weight, the full derivation is public at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/), and the challenge process is part of the design. Falsifiable is not a posture here; it is the mechanism.

If you work in agriculture, food & harvest, environmental & climate services, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it.
